rendered:
The question's premise does not match the paper. The paper does not conclude that aqueous processing is incompatible with the Ni-rich cathode. It concludes the opposite: Overall, this work clearly demonstrates that aqueous processing is compatible with Ni-rich NMC 811[1]

On leaching, the paper says the percentage of leached Li+ rises with nickel content, but that even the Ni-rich NMC cathode shows only minimal leaching, about ~3 wt%[2] over the test period. The supporting words are: even Ni-rich NMC 811 shows only minimal Li^þ[3].

The paper does note that aqueous-processed cells retain slightly less capacity than NMP-processed cells (~70%[4] versus ~76%[5]), but it judges that the aqueous-processed cells still cycle very well: the aqueous-processed NMC 811 cells still demonstrate very good cycling performance[6].

The paper also lists other issues that formulation must handle, such as Li/H+ exchange, a highly basic solvent pH, and modification of the cathode surface morphology. It treats these as challenges to manage, not as a barrier: There are several other issues that can arise with NMC 811 aqueous processing if formulation chemistry is not handled properly[7].

The word incompatible does not occur in the document.[8]
